thread.title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 30 Points as Apple Beats, Fed Clock Ticks

author: Barron's
title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 30 Points as Apple Beats, Fed Clock Ticks
text:
Want to know why the Dow Jones Industrial Average is doing what it's doing? Check back here for a semi-live look at the volatile markets from Barron's reporters.
Getty Images 6:48 a.m. It's Fed day and boy is the market...not doing much yet. S&P 500 futures have ticked up 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have advanced 29 points, or 0.1%, and Nasdaq Composite futures have risen 0.3%.
While all the focus is on the Fed--don't expect much from today's meting--we shouldn't forget that we're still in the heart of earnings season. Apple ( AAPL ) has gained3.3% to $174.93 in pre-open trading after its beat , and it's not the only company to be topping estimates. Credit Suisse strategist Jonathan Golub notes that earnings have risen at an 18% clip excluding tax benefits, and companies have been beating by 8%. Of course, the market hasn't been responding to the outstanding results, but Golub insists they should be. "Concerns surrounding peaking EPS and economic growth, rising inflation/rates, a flattening yield curve , and a maturing business cycle are weighing on stocks," Golub writes. "While each issue has merit, we believe investors are under-estimating the market's potential upside, and over-estimating risks."
Unless, of course, they're not.
